items.title: Can I use it for paid client work?
items.description: Yes. MIT licence, no attribution required, unlimited sites. Agencies ship it under their own brand — that is the most common use.

items.title: What do I need to start?
items.description: A current Node.js and a terminal. Run the create command, then `npm run dev`. Site name, URL and blog options live in one config file; colours and fonts in one styles file.

items.title: How do clients edit content after handover?
items.description: Markdown in the repo, or a CMS — adapters for Sanity, Contentful and Git-based editors are included. Content lives in collections, so a wrong edit fails the build instead of breaking the live site.

items.title: Is it GDPR-ready?
items.description: Consent gating analytics, a preferences dialog, and terms and privacy pages you fill in. Not legal advice — but the mechanics are there instead of a script tag firing on load.

items.title: Where can I deploy it?
items.description: Anywhere static files are served: Vercel, Netlify, Cloudflare, GitHub Pages, an nginx container or your own server. Presets included for the first four.
